desc: Correct the operation interpretation: both A and B swap adjacent blocks 0^X1^Y <-> 1^Y0^X (move a block of Y ones across X zeros); A moves ones left, B moves them right, and they are exact inverses.

Run the brute-force script and capture actual counterexamples for `(X,Y)=(1,2)` and `(2,2)`: invariant-matched split components, distinct A-normal forms in one component, and their linear gap/run tuples.
Test confluence: for every enumerated string, compute normal forms from multiple random A-rewrite orders and from leftmost-greedy/stack; report any differences.

If confluence holds, design an O(N) stack normalizer for `0^X1^Y -> 1^Y0^X` using run-length trailing state rather than suffix copying; otherwise use brute-force output to identify the missing invariant.
Validate the chunk/remainder hypothesis (`zero-run = qX+r`, `one-run = pY+s`) against components, especially how remainders at linear boundaries block movement.

Handle edge cases: S==T always Yes; zero ones or all ones; X+Y>N means no operation so Yes iff S==T; necessary invariant counts of ones per residue mod X (equivalently gaps mod X including leading/trailing) must match.
Validate any final criterion by exhaustive BFS for small parameters and by the provided samples before writing the final Python stdin/stdout solution.
